1.

The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 09.08.2024.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 09.08.2024 at about 7.00 a.m., within the jurisdiction of Bannerughatta Police Station, Bannerughatta - Jigani 3 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6314/2024 main road,
Ragihalli gate, Jigani Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bangalore District, when the Petitioner was riding unoffending Honda Dio vehicle bearing registration No.KA-51-HP-0795, the accused/driver of the offending Force Tempo Traveler vehicle bearing registration No.KA-06-AA-1481 drove the same in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result the rider/Petitioner of the unoffending vehicle fell down on the road and he has sustained grievous injuries and the accused left the spot without reporting the alleged incident.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.223/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 281 and 125(b) of BNS R/w Section 187 of MV Act and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.

Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he became permanently disabled and he is unable to do his work normally as he was doing prior to the occurrence of the alleged accident.

The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending Vehicle bearing registration No.KA-06-AA-1481 and Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the RC owner of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondents are Jagannath T vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. In the written statement of Respondent No.1, the Insurance Company has admitting that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denying the petition averments in part and contended that the Petitioner has not furnished the particulars of the vehicle including the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The insurer liability is subjected to validity of the DL, permit and other documents in accordance with law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158 of M.V. Act.
Further it is alleged that the alleged accident is occurred due to negligence and fault of the Petitioner and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age, income and occupation of the Petitioner and further the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimant is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V. Act., and the driver of the offending car did not possess the valid and effective driving licence as on the date of occurrence of the accident and violated terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

6 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6314/2024 :: I S S U E S ::

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 09.08.2024 at about 7.30 a.m., to 7.40 a.m.,
when he was riding the unoffending Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-51-HP-0795 to go to Venkateshwara Temple from Shivanahalli side on Ragihalli main road near Ragihalli gate and he turned his Motor Cycle with indication to go towards Jigani and turned right towards Bannergatta main road, at that time the driver of the offending TT Vehicle bearing registration No.KA-06- AA-1481 drove the same in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and came from Bannerghatta side and dashed against the Motor Cycle and due to impact he fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

from whom?
3.
What order or award?

sentences.text: The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.

Hence, in order to prove his case,
the Petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 and he has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in his evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.12 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.
I have gone through the documents produced by the PW-1.

Ex.P-1 is the True copy of FIR in Cr.No.223/2024, Ex.P-2 is the True copy of Statement/complaint dated 09.08.2024, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar dated 10.08.2024, Ex.P.4 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.5 is the Notice issued under Section 133 of MV Act to the owner of the offending vehicle, Ex.P.6 is the Reply to notice given by the owner of the offending vehicle, Ex.P.7 is the Motor vehicle Accident Report, Ex.P.8 is the Charge Sheet, Ex.P.9 is the Discharge Summary.
Ex.P.10 is the 13 Medical bills, Ex.P.11 is the Notarized copy of Aadhaar card and Ex.P.12 is the Notarized copy of D.L. card and 12.

In the cross-examination of PW-1 by Respondent No.1, he has deposed that he has given the complaint/statement to the police regarding the alleged accident at the time of taking treatment in the Hospital.

At the time of alleged accident he was riding the 10 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6314/2024 unoffending vehicle from Shivanahalli towards Jigani and the driver of the offending vehicle was coming from Bannerghatta.

At the spot the driver of the unoffending vehicle dashed against the hind portion of the unoffending vehicle and as a result front and back side of his vehicle was damaged and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Further he has denied that at the time of alleged accident he was trying to overtake the offending vehicle and he lost control over the same and due to his fault caused the alleged accident.
Further he has denied that he was not wearing helmet at the time of the alleged accident.
Further he has deposed that he has not undergone surgery.
Further he has denied that he has sustained simple injuries in the alleged accident.
Further he has denied that he has not taken treatment for the injuries sustained in the alleged accident and he has taken the treatment for some other incident.
Further he has deposed that he has not taken follow-up treatment.
Further he has denied that he has not incurred Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical, transportation and other expenses.
Further he has deposed that he has not produced documents to show that he was Priest and earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.
Further he has denied that he was not working as a Priest and not earning any income as alleged.
Further he has denied that he was hale and 11 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6314/2024 healthy and he was doing his regular activities as past without suffering any pain or difficulties.
Further he has denied that the alleged accident is occurred due to his fault and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further he has denied that he has produced concocted created documents and he is deposing falsely.
During the cross, examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition/prosecution case and he has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

sentences.text: The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Statement/Complaint, Ex.P3/Spot Mahazar, Ex.P-4/Wound Certificate and Ex.P-8/Charge Sheet clearly establishes that the alleged 15 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6314/2024 accident occurred at the spot.

It is not in dispute as to the aspect that,
the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P4/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road traffic accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused/driver.

Matters being so,
the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281 and 125(b) of BNS R/w Section 187 of MV Act.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent person/Petitioner aforesaid, as the accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly and negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

19. Issue No.2:- The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that the injured Petitioner was aged about 57 years and he was working as Priest at Temple and 16 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6314/2024 performing rituals and ceremonies and earning an income of Rs.40,000/- per month and the Petitioner has incurred Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenditure.

As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses, special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

20. On the other hand the learned counsel for Respondent No.1 insurance company contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about he was earning an income of Rs.40,000/- per month, the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents.
Since the Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.

21. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 57 years and he was working as Priest at Temple and performing rituals and ceremonies and earning an income of Rs.40,000/- per month.

The petitioner relied on the Ex.P.12/driving licence of the Petitioner and wherein the date of birth of 17 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6314/2024 the Petitioner is shown as 22.07.1967 and this accident was occurred on 09.08.2024.
Hence it is clear that on the strength of the Ex.P-12/driving licence as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 57 years.
Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 57 years.
22. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was working as Priest at Temple and performing rituals and ceremonies and earning an income of Rs.40,000/- per month.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2024, the notional income of the Petitioner taken at Rs.15,750/-.
23.

To prove the percentage of disability sustained by the Petitioner, neither the Petitioner got examined his treated doctor, nor produced disability certificate, hence the Petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under 18 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6314/2024 the head future loss of income on account of permanent disability.
24. As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as Priest at the temple and in the alleged accident the petitioner has sustained pulmonary contusion with hemothorax.
Further the doctor opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.
The injuries shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering, mental agony.
25. The Petitioner contended that, due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he took treatment as an inpatient at Vijayashree Hospital from 09.08.2024 to 12.08.2024.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head transportation, nourishment and other charges.
26. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.

27. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast three months period to 19 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6314/2024 recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.

Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.47,250/- (Rs.15,750/- p.m, X 3 months)
under the head loss of income during laid up period.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioner.
On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Spot Mahazar, MVA Report, Wound Certificate, Charge Sheet, Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, reply to the Notice U/sec.133 of 14 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.6314/2024 IMV Act, and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P4/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road traffic accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused/driver.
Matters being so,
the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281 and 125(b) of BNS R/w Section 187 of MV Act.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent person/Petitioner aforesaid, as the accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly and negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2024, the notional income of the Petitioner taken at Rs.15,750/-.
